title: Client-side validation vs trusted server validation
learningObjectives: Explain client-side validation vs trusted server validation and apply secure, accessible, maintainable browser practices.

understand.concept: Client-side validation improves feedback and reduces avoidable requests, but users can bypass it by editing the page or sending requests directly. The server must independently validate input, authenticate the actor, authorize the action, and enforce business rules.
understand.whyItMatters: Trusting client validation can expose data or privileged actions. Treat every client request as untrusted even when it originates from your own frontend.
understand.analogy: Client validation checks the form at the counter; server validation checks the request at the actual gate.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser security, accessibility, and performance rules depend on platform behaviour and server configuration.

explain.narrative: The regular expression checks the shape of one value only. It does not prove ownership, identity, or permission.

examples.code: function isValidCode(value){return /^[A-Z]{2}-\d{4}$/.test(value)}console.log(isValidCode('CS-2048'));// Server must validate again and authorize the requested operation.
examples.explanation: The regular expression checks the shape of one value only. It does not prove ownership, identity, or permission.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the security or reliability principle.

practise.guidedTask: List client-side usability checks and matching server-side security checks for an edit operation.
practise.independentTask: Review a small browser feature for security, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle risks. Add a fallback and document the server-side controls required.
hints: Treat all browser and network input as untrusted.
Use exact origin checks and least privilege.
Measure performance and clean up resources.
